name: r6b_tou_bank_lead_follows_primary_heat__v4
description: Heating mirror of r6b_tou_bank_lead_follows_primary__v4: a winter peak starts at 16:15, the house is at 71 F and banking toward the 76 F comfort ceiling means 5 F of heat. Primary engine v4 (v3 live as the comparison engine), a realistic 5 F per hour furnace (4.5 F in the first hour through the hidden mass), 30 F outside and a 0.05 leak: the lead comes from v4's OWN house model (thermal mass and sun included), stepped with the furnace fully on against the forecast, not from a first-order formula (Issue #1517). That model needs about 105 minutes (121 with the 1.15 safety factor), so the window opens at 14:14, 74 minutes after this scenario starts. The same house gives a different start under every other lead: v3's slow rate 12:15 (the 240-minute cap), the first-order leak formula on v4's rates 13:45 (150 minutes), the plain delta/rate formula 14:48. Nothing is banked before 14:14, and the thermostat is told 76 F at the 14:14:59 check, not at the 14:30 half-hour cycle.

assertions.reason: Before the window opens nothing is banked.
Until the window opens the thermostat is only told the 68 F comfort setpoint (the 13:00 setup and the 13:30 and 14:00 cycles).

The window the plan shows starts 121 minutes before the 16:15 peak, from v4's own house model: v3's rate would start at 12:15 (240-minute cap), the first-order leak lead at 13:45, the plain formula at 14:48.

The thermostat is told the 76 F bank setpoint at the first 5-minute check at or after the 14:14 window start (14:14:59), without the 68 F comfort setpoint first (issue #1393; the heating mirror), not at the 14:30 half-hour cycle.
The 14:30 cycle inside the open bank re-asserts the 76 F bank setpoint once, without the 68 F comfort setpoint first (issue #1393; the heating mirror).
Banking toward the 76 F comfort ceiling.
The plan list names the same 14:14 start the thermostat acted on.

verdict.summary: The heating bank opens by the primary engine (v4) house model, and the plan and thermostat agree on when
verdict.observed_behavior: Window 14:14 (v4's house model needs about 105 min raw, 121 min with the 1.15 safety factor); nothing banked before it; first 76 F written at the 14:14:59 check.
verdict.expected_behavior: Mirror of the cooling bank: the furnace is not run for hours more than the house needs before a peak price period, and the lead is v4's own house model (thermal mass, sun, leak), not a first-order formula (Issue #1517). Re-derived 2026-11-11 with the owner's approval (third re-derivation for #1517): the inputs changed (furnace 3.5 to 5 F per hour, hidden-mass coupling 0.6 to 0.3) so that v4's stepped lead lands inside the run, below the 240-minute cap, and this golden tells the engines apart again. The earlier inputs put every lead at the cap, identical to the v3 twin.
